A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Advantage Weighted Matching by the same authors. Their readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10/ImageNet-64 pretraining experiments and SD3.5M/FLUX reinforcement-learning results, including benchmark comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds revised-configuration benchmarks, sampler comparisons, direct target-variance measurements, and a qualitative diversity study.

M1.justification: The advantage-weighted DSM/FM framework remains. The later configuration changes loss weighting from w(t)=1 to w(t)=t, replaces the fixed reference model with an EMA reference, and adopts purely on-policy updates instead of mixed data reuse (Sections 3–4 and Appendix F.1). These refine the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Coverage remains CIFAR-10/ImageNet-64 pretraining and compositional generation, text rendering, and human-preference alignment. ImageReward adds a reward/evaluation model within the existing preference-alignment task; the PDFs do not establish a new dataset, domain, or task requirement.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds TempFlow-GRPO as a quantitative GenEval comparator, reporting 0.97 overall and 2.8× speedup. v1 only discusses it in related work. The other corresponding benchmark comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: The main configuration changes from Euler–Maruyama sampling, four training timesteps, mixed on/off-policy updates, and task-specific KL coefficients to SA-Solver, six Monte Carlo timesteps, on-policy updates, and KL coefficient 1. Appendix F.1 explicitly distinguishes the earlier and later sampling steps, noise levels, and guidance scales. New sampler controls are introduced, and GenEval ablations now report training steps instead of GPU hours.

E4.justification: v1's timestep-distribution, four-value KL, and previous-policy batch-reuse ablations are replaced by Monte Carlo count, EMA-rollout versus on-policy, and KL 1-versus-3 comparisons. v2 additionally tests ODE/SDE compatibility (Figure 8), measures conditional target variance (Table 6), and examines diversity after 600 RL steps (Figure 10). The original ablation plots are not retained in the appendices.

E5.justification: Figure 10 newly specifies four different initial-noise seeds per prompt for the qualitative diversity demonstration. This is limited seed reporting, rather than repeated-training-run uncertainty analysis; neither version provides benchmark confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Under revised settings, v2 reports final GenEval 0.985 and 16.54× speedup to Flow-GRPO's score, versus v1's 0.95 and 8.02×. SD3.5M PickScore changes from 23.02 at 91.1 GPU hours to 23.11 at 27.56 hours; OCR changes from 0.89 at 17.6 hours to 0.92 at 21.76 hours. These are different-configuration results. Original tables survive as Tables 4–5, and FLUX table values remain unchanged. New ImageReward, variance, ablation, and diversity results expand the evidence.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly frames Theorem 2.1 as an oracle, fixed-time population-minimizer equivalence. Appendix C.3 adds a substantial derivation connecting advantage-weighted DDPO's local gradient to clean-target DSM without assuming advantage independence from noisy states. Appendix C.5 derives the EDM noisy-target objective. The original DSM equivalence and variance proofs largely remain.

C1.justification: The three central DDPO–DSM, variance, and AWM contributions remain. The abstract and conclusion raise the headline speedup from 24× to 34×, while the introduction changes GenEval performance from matching Flow-GRPO to surpassing it. The contribution list also includes ImageReward.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies the oracle/population scope and practical discretization bias of the equivalence argument. It replaces discussion of logit-normal and weak-KL failures with interpretations supporting the revised defaults, and adds an interpretation of preserved diversity after 600 updates. The central explanation linking noisy targets to slower optimization remains.

D1.justification: Appendix F.1 documents both configurations systematically, adding previously unstated sampling noise and guidance settings, reference-model choices, the EMA schedule, and precise batch-use mechanics. Section 3 specifies batch-global advantage normalization. v1's explicit shared-noise/timestep disclosure for likelihood-ratio estimation disappears. The code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix E adds a substantive distinction between AWM's signed weights and classical RWR/AWR, plus discussion of continuous-time RL by Gao and Zhao. New citations support normalization and reference-model choices, while the LLaDA 1.5 citation is removed. Existing positioning against DDPO and FMPG largely remains.

P1.justification: Related work moves from the main text to Appendix E, bringing theory directly after the introduction. The DDPO exposition is extensively rewritten, notation and detailed-background sections are added, and the appendix is reorganized around proofs, related work, configurations, and additional experiments.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper. Figure 1's panels are rearranged, the ablation figure is replaced, sampler and diversity figures are added, and notation and variance tables appear. Earlier benchmark tables move to the appendix, while Figure 9 combines retained curves with an added ImageReward panel.

improvement.justification: v1 motivates advantage-weighted RL largely through unweighted DSM results; v2 adds an explicit local-gradient derivation and clearer oracle assumptions (Section 2.3 and Appendix C.3). Direct variance measurements, sampler tests, revised ablations, and detailed configuration documentation substantially strengthen the central argument and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removal of earlier ablations and remaining reporting inconsistencies, including Figure 1's 8× caption beside a 16.54× plot.
